Thank you for working on this patch Andrew. I've started reviewing it and it looks promising so far.
I do have a few initial comments which I'd like to share.
What is meant by area and images ? Should it be a part of package_header_information struct as it's not defined in the spec ?
Are we decoding vendor defined descriptors from the package?

Since this is not be present in PLDM package Version 1.0.x, I assume it's not tightly coupled and we should be able to parse the package descriptors and component information without using this foreach statement.

Could you please add a UT for the same ?
I was able to figure out the flow from the code but please consider adding an UT for the above case.

Looking into DSP0267_1.3.0.pdf, page 1011, 

Table 3 - PLDM Firmware Package Header

```
A value of 1244D2648D7D4718A030FC8A56587D5A shall indicate that the update package format
conforms to Version 1.1
```

I'm confused why the variable is named ```PLDM_FWUP_PACKAGE_HEADER_IDENTIFIER_V2_0```

In the entire document i cannot find anything when looking for ```Version 2```
and it seems to be the latest version of the document

https://www.dmtf.org/standards/pmci
Guessing that `2` comes from the value of `PackageHeaderFormatRevision`, but agree with Alexander, a more formal name decleration would be better.
@unive.tien.wiwynn@gmail.com yes, that's the explanation, but I will change it to be more intuitive.
what if it's 0, shouldn't we show an error?
do we log in libpldm, didn't see it anywhere else in the code ?

why do we need to repeat this checks again ? 
It's already validated in decode_pldm_package_header_info_errno() so this one is redundant.
Maybe the data would be assembled elsewhere, although this is out of libpldm expected?
Done

what does pldm_msgbuf_discard() return, is it rc?
This looks like a new addition, yet to go through all the patches but was curious to know.
@alexander.hansen@9elements.com yep. This helps ensure correct use of the msgbuf instance (errors are returned to the caller appropriately)

nit: Putting this constant in the middle of the file will make it harder to reorder and refactor functions later on.

It might just get lost or re-defined in such a long file.

If it's only needed for this one function, can it be defined as


```
const unsigned int PLDM_FWUP_DOWNSTREAM_DEVICE_ID_RECORD_MIN_SIZE = 11;
```

inside the function, to limit the scope.

If it's needed for multiple functions, maybe put it near the start of the file.

It is only needed for the single function, but defining it as `const unsigned int` means it's not an "integer constant expression" with respect to the C language (which then may affect constant propagation during optimisation). I'll leave it for now. Any incorrect refactoring due to the location will yield a compilation failure, so it's not going to trip anyone up for too long.

Picked up this patch to validate end-to-end package parsing alongside the PLDM integration changes. The positive path looks good.

One piece of feedback: we shouldn't mandate callers to invoke the foreach_pldm_downstream_device_id_record iterator for PLDM V1 packages, as it's not applicable in that context.
Keeping the thread open for now.

Hi all; there's still a bunch of comments outstanding, and there's still some thought needed for handling caller vs package version support, but I've taken this out of WIP for now after some reworks.
Thanks Andrew, just being here to leave my concern for supporting next DSP0267 revision.

There should be a `reference_manifest` here if we're referencing DSP0267 v1.3.0, otherwise an older revision should be linked.

Even it is optional(length can be 0), a 4-byte field is still used in the format for describing the length.

I understand the confusion there, but the v1.3.0 spec also encompasses the earlier package format revisions. We're only implementing up to package format revision 2 in this patch. Package format revision 3 can follow in a subsequent patch.

The package format pin concept that I've now introduced allows us (with a little bit of work) to append further members to these structs, which is an act that would otherwise break the ABI. Both sides (library implementation and library consumer) have to demonstrate that they agree on specific struct sizes for each package format revision. This ensures that changes are forwards and backwards compatible (in the sense that the library will either function as required or gracefully return an error, and not perform invalid memory accesses).
Same as above, `reference_manifest` for DSP0267 v1.3.0.
A `component_opaque_data` should be here if it is DSP0267 v1.3.0 revision.
